item.title: The new international education strategy settles the policy direction – now we need to make it work
item.description: International recruitment may no longer have a target attached, but it's going to remain a big part of the international agenda, argues IDP's Simon Emmett – so it needs to be backed up with evidence of quality and outcomes

item.title: What grade inflation panics miss about the real value of higher education
item.description: Mark Peace puts the case that pressure on the graduate premium, in combination with AI, should be causing higher education to look again at the challenge of capturing the full breadth of student outcomes, beyond a single grade

item.title: The forthcoming NHS workforce plan must treat universities as partners
item.description: A new 10-year workforce plan for the National Health Service ought to be an opportunity to think carefully about higher education’s role. Susanna Kalitowski explains

item.title: Direct entrant students can no longer remain invisible
item.description: The post-16 white paper wants a more flexible system. For Eloise Heathcote, this means tackling the challenges faced by students who join degrees in later years

item.title: What does the 2026 January deadline data show?
item.description: UCAS' Director of Data and Analysis picks out the key themes from the 2026 UCAS January Deadline data release

item.title: HESA Spring 2026: Student data
item.description: The first HESA data release of the season is upon us, so DK unwraps data that gives an insight into current policy topics of interest.

item.title: Scotland orders sector-wide assessment review after Glasgow QAA findings
item.description: Following the tragic death of a student, a new report identifies failures in academic governance at the University of Glasgow. Jim Dickinson examines the implications

item.title: Universities need to get a grip on reasonable adjustments
item.description: Jim Dickinson examines new research on access at universities, and asks why improved attitudes toward disabled students have yet to translate into reliable, systemic support

item.title: You can’t give students a voice. They already have one
item.description: Survey fatigue is real, trust is at an all-time low, and partnership frameworks often operate like consultation in disguise. Nikita Asnani explains why student voice needs to become structure, not just sound

item.title: A statutory duty of care won’t fix student safeguarding. Implementation will
item.description: Donny McCormick argues that universities already operate within a dense framework of responsibilities – and that adding another legal duty won't solve the real problems
